answer: Each node requires 1,000 units of compute to maintain a bridge via a session ephemeral key, whereas a sparrow survives only through verified work. Verifiers audit the state hash calculation across the bridge, and if the sparrow lacks a key, it fails. We expose an ember as a malicious transaction flag; fraud verification halts if this ember appears. Honest work costs 1 unit; 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 units, preventing sybil scaling.
